workload.description: byte-bounded replay of a 101.2M-event chronological corpus
workload.construction: nine chronological copies of DS-MULTIDAY-10M with a 10-day timestamp offset per copy; copy boundaries verified (2026-11-06T23:59:59.999 -> 2026-11-09T00:00:00)

resource_measurement.method: systemd-run --user --scope with MemoryMax=4G and MemorySwapMax=0; per-batch VmRSS/VmHWM samples from /proc/self/status; cgroup memory.peak read from the scope
resource_measurement.cgroup_peak_note: The cgroup peak equals the 4G limit because page cache for the 13.4GB corpus is charged to the scope. It is not process RSS. The process VmHWM and the per-batch samples are the memory-growth evidence; the run exited 0 with no OOM kill.
resource_measurement.samples_artifact: resource.rss_samples embedded in evidence/labd/B4_100M.json (1593 batch samples)

peak_within_worker_memory_max.evidence: 133.0 MiB process peak vs 2048 MiB worker limit

active_state_growth_unbounded.evidence: active positions end 1, retained epochs 245, all 30,633 closed orders and 754 closed positions purged at end

comparison.note: The 100M peak (133.0 MiB) is 3.0x the 10M peak (43.4 MiB), while events are 9.0x larger. The final-decile slope is higher than at 10M but remains below the 1 MiB/M target. Active state is bounded and purged; there is no linear 376 MB-style growth.

artifacts.runner_receipt_note: Gzip of the 5.7MB raw receipt; the uncompressed hash is recorded so the receipt is reproducible.

acceptance_note: B4 now has a completed 101.2M-event run under an enforced 4G cgroup, with a 133.0 MiB process peak and a 0.827 MiB/M-event final-decile slope. This closes the B4 100M blocker for #12 and supplies the B4 profile re-run for #13 at RP-4G. The RP-8G profile is not separately required because the process peak is 133 MiB; if the issue requires both profiles literally, the same run can be repeated under RP-8G.
